meaning: Remove pencil or chalk marks by rubbing them.
japanese: こすって消す。消しゴムで消す。
cue: You made a mistake in a pencil drawing.
reply: I rubbed out the last line and drew it again.
replyJapanese: 最後の線を消して、描き直しました。
transferCue: A teacher explains how to correct an answer sheet.
transferReply: If you change an answer, rub the old one out completely.
transferReplyJapanese: 答えを変えるときは、前の答えをきれいに消してください。
nuance: Separable: rub out the mark or rub it out. Mainly British; American English says erase.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる。rub out the mark とも rub it out とも言う。主にイギリス英語で、アメリカ英語では erase を使う。
contrast: Rub out removes the mark completely; cross out draws a line through it and leaves it on the page.
contrastJapanese: rub out は跡を完全に消す。cross out は線を引いて消すだけで、文字は紙に残る。

meaning: Be very busy doing a lot of different things.
japanese: あれこれと忙しく動き回る。
cue: A friend asks why you look so tired.
reply: I've been running around all day getting ready for the party.
replyJapanese: パーティーの準備で、一日中バタバタしてたんだ。
transferCue: Describe a colleague's morning before a big meeting.
transferReply: He spent the morning running around trying to find a projector.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼は午前中、プロジェクターを探してあちこち走り回っていました。
nuance: Usually in the continuous, often with an -ing form after it. British English also says run round.
nuanceJapanese: 進行形で使うことが多く、あとに -ing 形を続けることが多い。イギリス英語では run round とも言う。
contrast: Run around is hurrying from one job to another; hang around is staying in one place with nothing to do.
contrastJapanese: run around は用事から用事へ忙しく動くこと。hang around は何もせず同じ場所にいること。

meaning: Send something to an organisation by post or online.
japanese: （書類などを）送って提出する。
cue: A job advert gives a closing date.
reply: Please send in your application by the end of the month.
replyJapanese: 月末までに応募書類をお送りください。
transferCue: A radio programme asked listeners for holiday pictures.
transferReply: Hundreds of listeners sent their photos in after the programme.
transferReplyJapanese: 番組のあと、何百人ものリスナーが写真を送ってきました。
nuance: Separable: send in a form or send it in. The receiver is an organisation, a competition or a programme, not a friend.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる。send in a form とも send it in とも言う。送り先は友人ではなく、団体やコンテスト、番組など。
contrast: Send in is posting or emailing something to an organisation; hand in is giving it to someone in person.
contrastJapanese: send in は郵送やメールで団体に送ること。hand in は直接手渡して提出すること。

meaning: Sign your name to show that you have received something.
japanese: 受け取りのサインをする。
cue: A courier arrives with a parcel.
reply: Could you sign for this parcel, please?
replyJapanese: この荷物の受け取りにサインをお願いできますか。
transferCue: You were out when a delivery came.
transferReply: My neighbour signed for the package while I was at work.
transferReplyJapanese: 仕事で留守の間、隣の人がサインして荷物を受け取ってくれました。
nuance: Inseparable: sign for it, not sign it for. The object is the thing delivered, not the paper you write on.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できない。sign for it と言い、sign it for とは言わない。目的語は署名する紙ではなく、届いた物。
contrast: Sign for confirms that a delivery has arrived; sign up for means joining a course or a service.
contrastJapanese: sign for は配達物の受け取りを確認すること。sign up for は講座やサービスに申し込むこと。

meaning: Spend time sitting and doing very little.
japanese: 何もせずに、だらだら座って過ごす。
cue: Describe a lazy Sunday at home.
reply: We sat around all afternoon watching old films.
replyJapanese: 午後はずっと、古い映画を見ながらだらだら過ごしました。
transferCue: Urge your flatmates to deal with a broken boiler.
transferReply: We can't just sit around hoping the landlord will call.
transferReplyJapanese: 大家さんから電話が来るのを当てにして、ただ座っているわけにはいかないよ。
nuance: Often followed by an -ing form, and critical with just. British English also says sit about.
nuanceJapanese: あとに -ing 形を続けることが多く、just を伴うと批判的に響く。イギリス英語では sit about とも言う。
contrast: Sit around is spending time idle; sit down is simply the action of taking a seat.
contrastJapanese: sit around は何もせずに時間を過ごすこと。sit down は単に腰を下ろす動作。

meaning: Stay asleep while something noisy happens.
japanese: （物音などに）気づかずに眠り続ける。
cue: There was a loud storm last night.
reply: I slept through the whole storm and heard nothing.
replyJapanese: 嵐の間ずっと眠っていて、何も聞こえませんでした。
transferCue: Explain why you arrived late at the office.
transferReply: Sorry I'm late. I slept through my alarm again.
transferReplyJapanese: 遅れてすみません。また目覚ましに気づかず寝過ごしました。
nuance: Inseparable: sleep through it. The object is the noise or event, such as an alarm, a storm or a film.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できない。sleep through it の語順。目的語は目覚まし、嵐、映画など、音や出来事。
contrast: Sleep through is not being woken by something; sleep in is staying in bed late on purpose.
contrastJapanese: sleep through は何かがあっても目を覚まさないこと。sleep in はわざと遅くまで寝ていること。

meaning: Move apart from each other to cover a larger area.
japanese: （集まっていた人が）散らばる。広がる。
cue: A tour guide speaks to a group at a crowded viewpoint.
reply: Please spread out so everyone can see the valley.
replyJapanese: 皆さんが谷を見られるように、広がってください。
transferCue: Describe a search for a lost dog.
transferReply: We spread out across the park and called his name.
transferReplyJapanese: 私たちは公園中に散らばって、その犬の名前を呼びました。
nuance: The past form is also spread: we spread out. With an object it means opening something flat, as in spread out a map.
nuanceJapanese: 過去形も spread で、we spread out となる。目的語を取ると spread out a map のように「広げる」の意味。
contrast: Spread out is moving apart while staying one group; split up is dividing into separate groups.
contrastJapanese: spread out は一つの集団のまま間隔を空けること。split up は別々のグループに分かれること。

meaning: Spend time standing somewhere and doing very little.
japanese: 何もせずに、ぼんやり立っている。
cue: A delivery has arrived and colleagues are only watching.
reply: Stop standing around and help me carry these boxes.
replyJapanese: ぼんやり立っていないで、この箱を運ぶのを手伝ってください。
transferCue: Describe the wait before a concert began.
transferReply: We stood around in the cold for nearly an hour.
transferReplyJapanese: 私たちは寒い中、1時間近くただ立っていました。
nuance: Often critical: it suggests people should be doing something useful. British English also says stand about.
nuanceJapanese: 批判的に響くことが多く、何か役に立つことをすべきだという含みがある。イギリス英語では stand about とも言う。
contrast: Stand around is standing with nothing to do; stand by is being ready to act when needed.
contrastJapanese: stand around は何もせずに立っていること。stand by は必要なときに動けるよう待機すること。

meaning: Move a short distance away from something or someone.
japanese: 後ろに下がる。少し離れる。
cue: You are about to light fireworks in the garden.
reply: Everyone stand back while I light the fireworks.
replyJapanese: 花火に火をつけるから、みんな下がって。
transferCue: Describe a visitor looking at a huge painting.
transferReply: She stood back from the painting to see it properly.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は絵をきちんと見るために、少し後ろに下がりました。
nuance: No object; from introduces what you move away from. Common in warnings and safety instructions.
nuanceJapanese: 目的語は取らず、離れる対象は from で示す。警告や安全上の指示でよく使う。
contrast: Stand back is moving away a little; stand aside is moving to one side to let someone pass.
contrastJapanese: stand back は少し後ろに下がること。stand aside は人を通すために脇へよけること。

meaning: Begin your working life or a job in a particular way.
japanese: （ある仕事や立場から）キャリアを始める。
cue: Talk about a restaurant manager's first job.
reply: Our manager started out as a waiter in this restaurant.
replyJapanese: うちの店長は、このレストランのウェイターとして働き始めました。
transferCue: Give advice to a young colleague.
transferReply: When you're starting out, say yes to every chance to learn.
transferReplyJapanese: 駆け出しのうちは、学べる機会にはすべて手を挙げましょう。
nuance: No object. Start out as plus a job is the usual pattern, and it suggests that things changed later.
nuanceJapanese: 目的語は取らない。start out as＋職業 の形が普通で、その後に変化があったことを示唆する。
contrast: Start out is how you began your working life; start up means opening a new business.
contrastJapanese: start out は職業人生をどう始めたかを言う。start up は新しい事業を立ち上げること。

meaning: Stay in a place, job or school longer than usual or after others leave.
japanese: （ほかの人が去ったあとも）そのまま残る。
cue: Your language course ends on Friday.
reply: I'm staying on in Edinburgh for a week after the course.
replyJapanese: 講座が終わったあとも、1週間エディンバラに残ります。
transferCue: A colleague has reached retirement age.
transferReply: She agreed to stay on for another year as an adviser.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は顧問として、もう1年残ることに同意しました。
frame: Stay on in a place / as something
nuance: No object. In British English stay on at school means continuing after the age when you can leave.
nuanceJapanese: 目的語は取らない。イギリス英語の stay on at school は、義務教育の年齢を過ぎても学校に残ること。
contrast: Stay on can last weeks or years; stay behind is usually a short time after others go, as after a class.
contrastJapanese: stay on は数週間から数年に及ぶこともある。stay behind は授業のあとなど、ほかの人が帰ったあとに少し残ること。

meaning: Come out further than the edge or surface of something.
japanese: 突き出る。はみ出す。
cue: Warn a friend about their wallet on a busy street.
reply: Your wallet is sticking out of your back pocket.
replyJapanese: 財布が後ろのポケットからはみ出してるよ。
transferCue: Explain how you scratched your arm on a walk.
transferReply: A branch stuck out over the path and scratched my arm.
transferReplyJapanese: 小道に突き出ていた枝で、腕を引っかきました。
nuance: The past is stuck out. Of or from introduces the place; with an object it means pushing a body part forward, as in stick out your tongue.
nuanceJapanese: 過去形は stuck out。場所は of や from で示す。目的語を取ると stick out your tongue のように、体の一部を突き出す意味になる。
contrast: Stick out points forwards or sideways; stick up points upwards, as untidy hair does.
contrastJapanese: stick out は前や横に突き出ること。stick up は寝ぐせの髪のように上に突き立つこと。

meaning: Support and help each other, especially in difficult times.
japanese: （困ったときに）助け合う。団結する。
cue: Your family is going through a hard year.
reply: We'll be fine as long as we stick together.
replyJapanese: みんなで支え合っていれば、きっと大丈夫です。
transferCue: Describe a football team that lost its sponsor.
transferReply: The players stuck together when the club ran out of money.
transferReplyJapanese: クラブの資金が尽きたとき、選手たちは団結しました。
nuance: No object, and the subject is always plural. It can also mean simply staying close to each other in a crowd.
nuanceJapanese: 目的語は取らず、主語は必ず複数。人混みで離れずにいる、という文字どおりの意味でも使う。
contrast: Stick together is about people supporting each other; stick to means not changing a plan or a decision.
contrastJapanese: stick together は人どうしが支え合うこと。stick to は計画や決定を変えずに守ること。

meaning: Make someone feel very worried and nervous.
japanese: 強いストレスを与える。ひどく不安にさせる。
cue: A friend asks how your exam revision is going.
reply: These exams are really stressing me out.
replyJapanese: この試験のせいで、本当にストレスがたまってる。
transferCue: Explain why your brother takes the train to work.
transferReply: Driving in heavy traffic stresses my brother out.
transferReplyJapanese: 兄は渋滞の中を運転すると、ひどくストレスを感じるんです。
nuance: Informal, and the person goes in the middle: it stresses me out. The adjective is stressed out.
nuanceJapanese: くだけた表現で、人は it stresses me out のように間に置く。形容詞は stressed out。
contrast: Stress out is worry that builds up over time; freak out is a sudden strong reaction of fear or anger.
contrastJapanese: stress out は時間をかけて積み重なる不安。freak out は恐れや怒りによる突然の激しい反応。

meaning: Tell someone in authority about something bad another person did.
japanese: 言いつける。告げ口する。
cue: A child has broken a vase and speaks to her brother.
reply: Promise you won't tell on me for breaking the vase.
replyJapanese: 花瓶を割ったこと、言いつけないって約束して。
transferCue: Describe what happened in class today.
transferReply: Someone told on the boys who were copying homework.
transferReplyJapanese: 宿題を写していた男の子たちのことを、誰かが先生に言いつけました。
nuance: Inseparable: tell on him, not tell him on. Informal and used mostly by or about children; adults say report.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できない。tell on him と言い、tell him on とは言わない。主に子どもが使う、または子どもについて使うくだけた表現で、大人は report を使う。
contrast: Tell on is reporting someone's bad behaviour; tell off is speaking angrily to someone because of it.
contrastJapanese: tell on は人の悪い行いを言いつけること。tell off はその行いを叱りつけること。

meaning: Make someone feel very tired.
japanese: へとへとに疲れさせる。
cue: You come home after a day in the hills.
reply: That long walk in the hills really tired me out.
replyJapanese: 丘を長く歩いたので、すっかり疲れ果てました。
transferCue: A grandparent talks about looking after the children.
transferReply: The grandchildren are lovely, but they tire us out by lunchtime.
transferReplyJapanese: 孫たちはかわいいのですが、お昼にはもうこちらがへとへとです。
nuance: Separable, and a pronoun goes in the middle: tire me out. The adjective tired out means completely tired.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる。代名詞は tire me out のように間に置く。形容詞 tired out は「疲れ切った」の意味。
contrast: Tire out is used about people and animals; wear out is a little stronger and is also used for things, like shoes.
contrastJapanese: tire out は人や動物に使う。wear out はやや強く、靴など物がすり切れる場合にも使う。

meaning: Stay in a place doing nothing while you wait for something.
japanese: 何もせずに、ただ待っている。
cue: Your flight was delayed with no new departure time.
reply: We waited around at the airport for five hours.
replyJapanese: 空港で5時間、何もできずに待ちました。
transferCue: A friend is very late and you decide to leave.
transferReply: I'm not waiting around for him any longer.
transferReplyJapanese: これ以上、彼をぼんやり待つつもりはないよ。
nuance: Use for before the person or thing. It sounds bored or annoyed; British English also says wait about.
nuanceJapanese: 待つ相手や物は for で示す。退屈やいら立ちの響きがあり、イギリス英語では wait about とも言う。
contrast: Wait around stresses the empty time with nothing to do; wait for is neutral and simply names what you expect.
contrastJapanese: wait around はすることのない待ち時間を強調する。wait for は中立的で、待つ対象を示すだけ。

meaning: Remove a mark or colour by washing, or disappear when washed.
japanese: （汚れや色を）洗い落とす。洗って落ちる。
cue: You spilled coffee on a white shirt.
reply: I hope this coffee stain washes out of my shirt.
replyJapanese: このコーヒーのしみ、シャツから落ちるといいのですが。
transferCue: Explain why a child's trousers are still green at the knees.
transferReply: I couldn't wash the grass stains out of his trousers.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼のズボンについた草のしみは、洗っても落とせませんでした。
frame: Wash something out / wash out of something
nuance: Works with or without an object: the stain washed out, or I washed the stain out. Of introduces the cloth.
nuanceJapanese: 目的語があってもなくても使える。the stain washed out とも I washed the stain out とも言う。布地は of で示す。
contrast: Wash out removes a mark from inside the cloth; wash off removes dirt sitting on a surface, like mud on boots.
contrastJapanese: wash out は布にしみ込んだ汚れを落とすこと。wash off は長靴の泥のように、表面についた汚れを洗い流すこと。

meaning: Look carefully and wait for someone or something to appear.
japanese: （現れるのを）注意して待つ。見張る。
cue: Ask a friend to help while you buy bus tickets.
reply: Can you watch for the bus while I buy the tickets?
replyJapanese: 切符を買っている間、バスが来ないか見ていてくれる？
transferCue: Describe a child waiting for a parent to come home.
transferReply: She stood at the gate, watching for her father's car.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は門のところに立って、父親の車が来るのを待っていました。
nuance: Inseparable: watch for it. The thing has not appeared yet; watch out for is similar but warns of danger.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できない。watch for it の語順。対象はまだ現れていない。watch out for は似ているが、危険への注意を促す。
contrast: Watch for is waiting for something to appear; look for is actively searching for something you cannot find.
contrastJapanese: watch for は何かが現れるのを待つこと。look for は見つからないものを自分から探すこと。

meaning: Write something on paper in full, with all the details.
japanese: （必要なことを）省かずに書く。書き出す。
cue: A friend loved your soup and wants to make it.
reply: I'll write the recipe out for you before you leave.
replyJapanese: 帰る前に、レシピを全部書いて渡しますね。
transferCue: Describe the end of a visit to the doctor.
transferReply: The doctor wrote out a prescription and handed it to me.
transferReplyJapanese: 医師は処方箋を書いて、私に手渡しました。
nuance: Separable: write out a list or write it out. Common with cheques, prescriptions, lists and recipes, and with in full.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる。write out a list とも write it out とも言う。小切手、処方箋、リスト、レシピなどによく使い、in full を添えることも多い。
contrast: Write out is writing the whole thing in full; write down is quickly noting something so you do not forget it.
contrastJapanese: write out は全体を省かずに書くこと。write down は忘れないようにさっと書き留めること。

meaning: From the very beginning of a period of time.
japanese: 最初からずっと。
cue: A colleague's early warning turned out to be correct.
reply: It turns out our accountant was right all along.
replyJapanese: 結局、うちの会計士は最初から正しかったわけです。
transferCue: You discover that friends planned a surprise party.
transferReply: So you knew about the party all along and said nothing!
transferReplyJapanese: じゃあ、パーティーのことは最初から知ってて黙ってたんだね！
nuance: Goes at the end of the clause, usually with know, be right or suspect. It often reveals something that was hidden or unnoticed until now.
nuanceJapanese: 節の最後に置き、know、be right、suspect などと使うことが多い。今まで隠れていた、あるいは気づかれていなかった事実を明かす場面でよく使う。

meaning: Used to say that something is still true despite what was just said.
japanese: それでもやはり。とはいえ。
cue: A neighbour offers you a lift you don't need.
reply: I'd rather walk, but thank you all the same.
replyJapanese: 歩いて行くので結構です。でも、お気遣いありがとうございます。
transferCue: You think a small risk still deserves care.
transferReply: The risk is small. All the same, I'd read the contract again.
transferReplyJapanese: リスクは小さいです。それでも、私なら契約書をもう一度読みます。
nuance: It starts or ends the sentence, usually set off by a comma. It's all the same to me is a different use and means I don't mind.
nuanceJapanese: 文頭か文末に置き、ふつうコンマで区切る。It's all the same to me は別の用法で、「どちらでもかまわない」の意味。

meaning: Considered as one complete group, not as separate parts.
japanese: 全体として。
cue: One region had a bad quarter.
reply: Sales fell in Europe, but the company as a whole grew.
replyJapanese: ヨーロッパでは売上が落ちましたが、会社全体としては成長しました。
transferCue: Summarise a set of exam results.
transferReply: Taken as a whole, the results are better than last year's.
transferReplyJapanese: 全体として見れば、今年の結果は昨年より良くなっています。
nuance: It usually comes straight after the noun: society as a whole. On the whole is different and means generally.
nuanceJapanese: society as a whole のように、名詞の直後に置くのが普通。on the whole は別の表現で、「概して」の意味。

meaning: Relaxed and comfortable, not nervous.
japanese: くつろいで。気楽に。
cue: Describe a kind interviewer.
reply: She smiled and put me at ease straight away.
replyJapanese: 彼女はにっこり笑って、すぐに私の緊張をほぐしてくれました。
transferCue: Talk about visiting your partner's family.
transferReply: I never feel completely at ease with his parents.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼の両親といると、どうしても完全にはくつろげません。
nuance: No article: at ease, not at an ease. Common after feel and in put someone at ease; the opposite is ill at ease.
nuanceJapanese: 冠詞は付けない。feel のあとや put someone at ease の形でよく使う。反対は ill at ease。

meaning: Feeling calm and not worried about anything.
japanese: 心が穏やかで。安らかな気持ちで。
cue: Say how you feel when you walk by the sea.
reply: I always feel at peace when I walk along the beach.
replyJapanese: 浜辺を歩いていると、いつも心が安らぎます。
transferCue: Describe a friend after a difficult decision.
transferReply: He seems at peace with his decision to retire early.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼は早期退職という決断を、穏やかに受け入れているようです。
nuance: No article. At peace with a decision means accepting it calmly; said of the dead, it is a gentle way to say someone has died.
nuanceJapanese: 冠詞は付けない。at peace with a decision は、決断を穏やかに受け入れているという意味。亡くなった人について言うと、死を遠回しに表す。

meaning: Using a particular method, tool or system.
japanese: 〜によって。〜を用いて。
cue: Explain how staff get into a secure building.
reply: Staff enter the building by means of an electronic card.
replyJapanese: 職員は電子カードを使って建物に入ります。
transferCue: Describe how supplies used to reach a mountain village.
transferReply: Supplies reached the village by means of a narrow mountain railway.
transferReplyJapanese: 物資は、細い山岳鉄道によって村に届いていました。
nuance: Formal and mostly written; in conversation by, with or using is more natural. Means keeps its s even for one method.
nuanceJapanese: 改まった表現で、主に書き言葉。会話では by、with、using のほうが自然。方法が一つでも means の s は落とさない。

meaning: Used to say what someone's character is naturally like.
japanese: 生まれつき。もともとの性格として。
cue: Explain why a colleague said nothing in the meeting.
reply: He's quiet by nature, so don't take his silence personally.
replyJapanese: 彼はもともと無口な性格なので、黙っていても気にしないでください。
transferCue: Describe yourself in a job interview.
transferReply: I'm not a risk-taker by nature, but I enjoy a challenge.
transferReplyJapanese: もともと冒険するたちではありませんが、難しい課題に挑むのは好きです。
nuance: No article and no possessive: by nature, not by my nature. It follows an adjective or noun, or opens the sentence.
nuanceJapanese: 冠詞も所有格も付けない。by my nature とは言わない。形容詞や名詞のあと、または文頭に置く。

meaning: Surprise someone when they are not ready or expecting it.
japanese: 不意を突く。
cue: An interviewer asked something you had not prepared for.
reply: The question about salary caught me off guard.
replyJapanese: 給与についての質問に、不意を突かれました。
transferCue: Describe a sudden change in the weather on a hike.
transferReply: We were caught off guard by how quickly the fog came down.
transferReplyJapanese: 霧があまりに急に下りてきて、私たちは不意を突かれました。
nuance: The person goes between catch and off guard. The passive be caught off guard is just as common.
nuanceJapanese: 人は catch と off guard の間に置く。受け身の be caught off guard も同じくらいよく使う。

meaning: Become lively, exciting or interesting.
japanese: 活気づく。生き生きとしてくる。
cue: Recommend the best time to visit a seaside town.
reply: The harbour really comes to life when the evening market opens.
replyJapanese: 夕方の市場が開くと、港は一気に活気づきます。
transferCue: Praise a history teacher.
transferReply: History came to life in her lessons through letters and diaries.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女の授業では、手紙や日記を通して歴史が生き生きとよみがえりました。
nuance: No article before life. To name the cause, use bring something to life: the photos bring the story to life.
nuanceJapanese: life に冠詞は付けない。きっかけを言うときは bring something to life を使う（the photos bring the story to life）。

meaning: Start to think sensibly again after behaving foolishly.
japanese: 分別を取り戻す。目を覚ます。
cue: A friend almost quit a good job after a small argument.
reply: I'm glad you came to your senses before you resigned.
replyJapanese: 辞める前に目を覚ましてくれて、よかったよ。
transferCue: Hope that a relative will give up an expensive hobby.
transferReply: I hope he comes to his senses and sells that old boat.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼が目を覚まして、あの古いボートを売ってくれるといいのですが。
nuance: Senses is always plural, and the possessive changes with the subject: my, his, their. It implies the earlier behaviour was foolish, so it can sound critical.
nuanceJapanese: senses は必ず複数形で、所有格は主語に合わせて my、his、their と変わる。それまでの行動が愚かだったという含みがあり、批判的に響くことがある。

meaning: Cause something to happen or exist.
japanese: 〜を引き起こす。〜を生じさせる。
cue: A vague email confused the whole team.
reply: The unclear wording gave rise to a lot of confusion.
replyJapanese: あいまいな言い回しが、多くの混乱を招きました。
transferCue: Report on a project that is running late.
transferReply: The delay has given rise to rumours that the project is cancelled.
transferReplyJapanese: この遅れから、計画が中止になったといううわさが生まれています。
nuance: Formal, typical of reports and news. No article before rise, and the result is usually a problem, a feeling or a rumour.
nuanceJapanese: 改まった表現で、報告書やニュースに多い。rise に冠詞は付けない。結果は問題、感情、うわさなどが多い。

meaning: Break or fall down suddenly under weight or pressure.
japanese: （重みや圧力で）崩れる。壊れる。
cue: An old chair broke during dinner.
reply: One leg of the chair gave way when he sat down.
replyJapanese: 彼が座ったとたん、椅子の脚が1本折れました。
transferCue: Warn friends walking on a frozen lake.
transferReply: The ice could give way if we walk any further out.
transferReplyJapanese: これ以上先まで歩くと、氷が割れるかもしれません。
nuance: No object and no article. In British English give way also means letting other traffic go first; American English says yield.
nuanceJapanese: 目的語も冠詞も取らない。イギリス英語では、ほかの車に道を譲る意味でも使い、アメリカ英語では yield と言う。

meaning: Be so obvious that it does not need to be said.
japanese: 言うまでもない。
cue: Remind your team that a client's details are confidential.
reply: It goes without saying that this stays within the team.
replyJapanese: 言うまでもなく、この件はチーム内にとどめてください。
transferCue: Tell a close friend they can always stay with you.
transferReply: It should go without saying, but you're always welcome here.
transferReplyJapanese: 言うまでもないことだけど、いつでも歓迎だよ。
nuance: The subject is almost always it, followed by a that-clause. People use it just before saying the obvious thing anyway.
nuanceJapanese: 主語はほぼ必ず it で、that 節が続く。当たり前のことを、あえて言う直前に使う。

meaning: Have the qualities or skills needed to succeed.
japanese: （成功に）必要な資質を備えている。
cue: Encourage a nervous new team leader.
reply: You clearly have what it takes to lead this team.
replyJapanese: あなたには、このチームを率いる力が間違いなくあります。
transferCue: Comment on young players hoping for a career in sport.
transferReply: Not every talented player has what it takes to turn professional.
transferReplyJapanese: 才能のある選手がみな、プロになれるだけの資質を備えているわけではありません。
frame: Have what it takes to do something
nuance: Usually followed by to plus a verb. The word it stays whatever the subject is: they have what it takes.
nuanceJapanese: あとに to＋動詞を続けることが多い。主語が何であっても it は変えない（they have what it takes）。

meaning: Used to say what really happens, not what is supposed to happen.
japanese: 実際には。現実には。
cue: Explain your office hours to a new colleague.
reply: Officially we finish at five, but in practice everyone stays later.
replyJapanese: 規則上は5時終業ですが、実際にはみんなもっと遅くまで残っています。
transferCue: Comment on a recycling scheme that sounds good.
transferReply: The scheme sounds simple, though it rarely works in practice.
transferReplyJapanese: その制度は単純に聞こえますが、実際にはめったにうまくいきません。
nuance: Often set against in theory, officially or on paper. No article; British English spells the noun practice and the verb practise.
nuanceJapanese: in theory、officially、on paper などと対比して使うことが多い。冠詞は付けない。イギリス英語では名詞を practice、動詞を practise とつづる。

meaning: Used to show which part of a subject you are talking about.
japanese: 〜の点では。〜に関しては。
cue: Compare two flats you have just viewed.
reply: In terms of location, the smaller flat is much better.
replyJapanese: 立地の点では、小さいほうの物件がずっといいです。
transferCue: Review the past year for a small business.
transferReply: It was our best year in terms of new customers.
transferReplyJapanese: 新規顧客の数で言えば、これまでで最高の年でした。
nuance: Followed by a noun or an -ing form, and terms is always plural. It is overused in business talk; often for or about is enough.
nuanceJapanese: あとに名詞か -ing 形を続け、terms は必ず複数形。ビジネスの場で多用されがちで、for や about で足りることも多い。

meaning: Without success or without the result you wanted.
japanese: 無駄に。むなしく。
cue: You could not find your keys this morning.
reply: I searched in vain for my keys for half an hour.
replyJapanese: 30分も鍵を探しましたが、見つかりませんでした。
transferCue: Reassure a team that lost a bid.
transferReply: Your hard work was not in vain, even though we lost the bid.
transferReplyJapanese: 入札には負けましたが、皆さんの努力は無駄ではありませんでした。
frame: Try in vain to do something
nuance: Slightly formal. It goes after the verb, as in tried in vain to…, or after be, as in it was not in vain.
nuanceJapanese: やや改まった表現。tried in vain to… のように動詞のあとか、it was not in vain のように be のあとに置く。

meaning: Change or develop at the same speed as something else.
japanese: （変化や進歩に）遅れずについていく。
cue: Talk about salaries and rising rents.
reply: Our wages haven't kept pace with rents in this city.
replyJapanese: この街では、賃金が家賃の上昇に追いついていません。
transferCue: Explain a problem for small shops.
transferReply: Small shops struggle to keep pace with changes in online shopping.
transferReplyJapanese: 小さな店は、ネット通販の変化についていくのに苦労しています。
nuance: No article before pace, and with introduces what you are matching. More formal than keep up with, and common in news about prices and technology.
nuanceJapanese: pace に冠詞は付けず、合わせる対象は with で示す。keep up with より改まった表現で、物価や技術のニュースでよく使う。

meaning: Spend time alone and avoid mixing with other people.
japanese: 人付き合いを避ける。一人で過ごすことが多い。
cue: Describe a quiet new neighbour.
reply: Our new neighbour is polite but keeps to himself.
replyJapanese: 新しいお隣さんは礼儀正しいのですが、あまり人付き合いをしません。
transferCue: Talk about your first term at university.
transferReply: I kept to myself during my first term at university.
transferReplyJapanese: 大学の最初の学期は、ほとんど一人で過ごしていました。
nuance: The reflexive matches the subject: he keeps to himself. With an object, keep something to yourself means not telling anyone.
nuanceJapanese: 再帰代名詞は主語に合わせる（he keeps to himself）。目的語を入れた keep something to yourself は「誰にも言わない」の意味。

meaning: Suddenly become too afraid to do something you planned.
japanese: 怖じ気づく。土壇場で勇気をなくす。
cue: You planned to ask your manager for more money.
reply: I meant to ask for a pay rise, but I lost my nerve.
replyJapanese: 昇給をお願いするつもりでしたが、土壇場で怖じ気づいてしまいました。
transferCue: Encourage a friend just before a speech.
transferReply: Don't lose your nerve now. You've practised this speech for weeks.
transferReplyJapanese: 今さら怖じ気づかないで。このスピーチ、何週間も練習してきたじゃない。
nuance: Nerve is singular and means courage; plural nerves means anxiety. The possessive changes with the subject: I lost my nerve.
nuanceJapanese: ここでの nerve は単数形で「勇気」の意味。複数形の nerves は「不安、緊張」。所有格は主語に合わせる（I lost my nerve）。

meaning: Become very successful, especially in a difficult career.
japanese: 成功する。（厳しい世界で）大成する。
cue: Talk about a friend who moved abroad to act.
reply: She moved to London, hoping to make it as an actor.
replyJapanese: 彼女は俳優として成功することを夢見て、ロンドンに移りました。
transferCue: Explain how hard the music business is.
transferReply: Very few bands ever make it in the music business.
transferReplyJapanese: 音楽業界で成功できるバンドは、ごくわずかです。
frame: Make it as something / in something
nuance: The word it is fixed and refers to nothing. Use as before a job and in before a field; the same phrase can also mean arriving in time or surviving.
nuanceJapanese: it は固定で、何も指さない。職業の前は as、分野の前は in。同じ形で「間に合う」「生き延びる」の意味にもなる。

meaning: End a quarrel with someone and become friendly again.
japanese: 仲直りする。和解する。
cue: Two brothers had not spoken for years.
reply: The brothers finally made peace at their mother's birthday party.
replyJapanese: 兄弟は、母親の誕生日パーティーでようやく仲直りしました。
transferCue: Advise a friend who fell out with a flatmate.
transferReply: You should make peace with her before she moves out.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女が引っ越す前に、仲直りしたほうがいいよ。
nuance: No article: make peace, not make a peace. With introduces the other person; make your peace with something means accepting a bad situation.
nuanceJapanese: 冠詞は付けない。make a peace とは言わない。相手は with で示す。make your peace with something は、好ましくない状況を受け入れるという意味。
